slides.title: EZRA Launches Loop for Connected Human and AI Coaching
slides.highlight: The launch of Loop, a connected human and AI coaching experience, aligns with MOSAIC's focus on adaptive AI coaching to improve human proficiency.

slides.title: FraudSociety: A Generative Agent-Based Society for the Financial-Fraud Economy
slides.highlight: FraudSociety introduces an LLM-agent-based simulator that jointly models informational and financial dynamics in fraud economies, offering a scalable testbed for evaluating interventions. This aligns with MIMIC's goal of simulating societal-scale interactions and impacts within hybrid human-AI systems.

card.one_liner: FraudSociety is the first LLM-agent simulator jointly modeling informational and financial dynamics of fraud.
card.key_idea: Integrates dynamic social graphs, persistent financial ledgers, and a Need-Intent-Action architecture to couple information exposure with financial outcomes.
card.evaluation: Validated via Quartet Distance against FTC stats and CAFC loss concentration; ablations confirm mechanism necessity; interventions show personalized warnings reduce repeat payments.
card.limitation: Small scale (112 civilians, 8 fraudsters) and reliance on Qwen3-14B may limit generalizability and computational efficiency.

slides.title: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control
slides.highlight: This work proposes training agents against simulated partners constrained by human physiological limits, offering a scalable alternative to expensive live feedback for improving zero-shot coordination in human-machine teaming.

card.one_liner: Training agents against cognitively constrained partners improves zero-shot coordination robustness in partitioned control.
card.key_idea: Simulates human-like partners using procedural physiological constraints (reaction delays, Weber's law) instead of reward shaping or historical checkpoints.
card.evaluation: Modified Lunar Lander; compared against FCP, PBT, MARL via cross-play and behavioral validation against 20 human players.
card.limitation: Human study pending; cross-play generalization not yet validated with real humans; constrained partners lack teammate action awareness.

slides.title: Realbotix Launches Echo Humanoid Robot Line
slides.highlight: Realbotix has introduced the Echo humanoid robot line, featuring tabletop and full-body models designed for social engagement, which aligns with HyECHO's focus on observing hybrid human-AI team dynamics.

slides.title: Simulation-Efficient Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation for Agent-Based Models
slides.highlight: DF-NPE reduces the computational cost of Bayesian parameter inference in agent-based models by 90% through synthetic data augmentation, supporting scalable simulation of complex societal dynamics.

card.one_liner: DF-NPE reduces agent-based model simulation costs by 90% using synthetic data augmentation for neural posterior estimation.
card.key_idea: Combines learned time-series summaries with two conditional normalizing flows to generate synthetic training pairs, supplementing expensive direct simulations.
card.evaluation: Tested on Brock-Hommes asset-pricing models using Wasserstein distance and MMD against likelihood-based ground truths; showed lower discrepancy and runtime than standard NPE.
card.limitation: Performance varies with synthetic-to-direct data allocation and training strategy; synthetic data quality depends on surrogate accuracy and representation stability.

slides.title: Multimodal Socially Aware Framework for Human-Robot Interaction in Virtual Reality
slides.highlight: This study evaluates a multimodal framework integrating speech, vision, and touch for social robots, revealing that autonomous systems still lag behind human-teleoperated baselines in naturalness and social appropriateness. It identifies conversational timing and spatial coordination as critical challenges for embodied social interaction.

card.one_liner: A multimodal framework integrating speech, vision, and touch for socially aware robot interaction in VR.
card.key_idea: Uses a VLM to process speech, vision, and touch inputs, generating coordinated robot movements and speech via interaction history.
card.evaluation: VR study with 18 participants across five scenarios, comparing autonomous system against human-teleoperated baseline using ratings and behavioral coding.
card.limitation: Autonomous system lagged behind teleoperated baseline in naturalness and appropriateness due to conversational timing and spatial coordination issues.

slides.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a multi-agent RL framework where a human model and exoskeleton policy co-adapt in simulation, achieving metabolic cost reduction in new users without per-user tuning. It aligns with MOSAIC's focus on coadaptive loops and physics-based proficiency estimation by showing how simulation-trained policies can transfer to real-world human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: Simulation-trained multi-agent RL hip exoskeleton reduces user metabolic cost without per-person tuning.
card.key_idea: Co-adaptive MARL trains a full-body human model and exoskeleton policy jointly, optimizing for physiological muscle metabolic power.
card.evaluation: Validated in eight adults via indirect calorimetry; showed 18.3% reduction vs passive and 7.4% vs no-exoskeleton walking.
card.limitation: High variance in no-exoskeleton comparison (±10.0%) and reliance on simulation fidelity for transfer to diverse users.

slides.title: From Belief Inference to Task Action: A Multi-Level Evaluation of Theory of Mind on Verifiable Tasks
slides.tldr: BRIDGING THEORY OF MIND AND ACTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multi-level evaluation framework that separates theory-of-mind inference from task execution, demonstrating that models often fail to translate correct belief recovery into optimal collaborative actions. This aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goal of ensuring AI teammates not only infer partner intent but also act effectively on those inferences in ad-hoc human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Multi-level evaluation reveals that correct belief inference does not guarantee successful task coordination in LLMs.
card.key_idea: Extends verifiable household and scheduling tasks with asymmetric information to independently assess world understanding, belief recovery, decision-making, and execution.
card.evaluation: Tested six LLMs on C-WAH and CalBench using paired controls; results show significant divergence between belief accuracy and task success rates.
card.limitation: Limited to six model configurations and specific simulated domains; lacks statistical significance from repeated runs or real-world collaboration data.

slides.title: Agent-Based Transport Model Calibration via Online Stochastic Batch Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces an online calibration framework for agent-based models that integrates stochastic batch optimization into the simulation loop, enabling real-time parameter co-evolution. It is relevant to MIMIC's goal of scalable, multi-scale simulation of hybrid societies by reducing the computational burden of calibrating complex agent behaviors.

card.one_liner: Calibrates agent-based transport models within a single simulation run using online stochastic batch optimization.
card.key_idea: Embeds calibration into MATSim iterations, treating replanning agents as stochastic batches to update utility parameters incrementally.
card.evaluation: Validated on a large-scale Swiss transport scenario; mode shares converged to observed data within typical simulation timeframes.
card.limitation: Relies on a quasi-static assumption that choice variables remain stable between iterations, which may fail in highly dynamic networks.

slides.title: Who Knows What - and What Does It Support? Perspective-Bounded Evidence Calibration for Multimodal Theory of Mind
slides.highlight: This work addresses perspective leakage in Theory of Mind by introducing PIP-ToM, an interface that calibrates evidence based on agent accessibility, directly supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of accurate intent inference in human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: PIP-ToM calibrates multimodal Theory of Mind inference by restricting evidence to agent-accessible, claim-relevant sources.
card.key_idea: Constructs agent-specific evidence stores and applies route-based calibration factors to Bayesian hypothesis scores, preventing perspective leakage.
card.evaluation: Outperforms baselines on MuMA-ToM, MMToM-QA, and Hi-ToM with GPT-4o, achieving 92-95% accuracy; ablations confirm component necessity.
card.limitation: Structured evidence matching alone fails for latent or recursive mental states, requiring underlying Bayesian inference for full accuracy.

slides.title: Context-Aware Generation and Modulation of Expressive Motion Behavior using Multimodal Foundation Models
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how multimodal foundation models can generate context-aware, expressive full-body gestures for robots, directly supporting the development of engaging embodied social interactions.

card.one_liner: Context-aware expressive robot motion generation using multimodal foundation models and knowledge distillation.
card.key_idea: Generates and modulates full-body gestures via Dynamic Movement Primitives, using distilled multimodal models for context-aware parameterization.
card.evaluation: User study with Pepper robot compared against non-modulated and API-level baselines; demonstrated cross-morphology versatility and reduced latency.
card.limitation: Relies on pre-recorded gesture libraries and may lack true open-ended motion generation beyond existing skill sets.

slides.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition
slides.highlight: This study compares structured reasoning against multimodal enrichment for resolving ambiguous instructions in human-robot interaction, finding that reasoning performs equally well when scene information is already textual. This informs RwB's approach to handling pragmatic intent in embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Synthetic multimodal enrichment offers no benefit over structured reasoning for pragmatic intent recognition.
card.key_idea: CEMIR enriches text with generated narratives/images; FISER uses structured social/embodied reasoning on raw text.
card.evaluation: Compared on HandMeThat v2 (400 episodes) across 4 LLMs; statistical tests showed no significant performance difference.
card.limitation: Findings may not generalize to tasks where ambiguity stems from missing observable scene information.

slides.title: EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
slides.highlight: EvolveMAS demonstrates test-time adaptation and experience reuse in decentralized multi-agent systems through a dedicated MemoryAgent, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that adapt beyond in-context learning and self-correct via meta-cognitive memory governance.

card.one_liner: EvolveMAS enables decentralized multi-agent self-evolution via memory governance and cross-episode knowledge reuse.
card.key_idea: Pairs agents with external MemoryAgents to maintain structured memory, supporting within-episode adaptation and cross-episode strategy distillation.
card.evaluation: Tested on five benchmarks across cooperative, mixed-motive, and adversarial settings; achieved highest average score of 77.2.
card.limitation: Requires dedicated external memory agents, potentially increasing computational overhead and complexity compared to self-managed memory.

slides.title: Navigating human-robot interaction challenges in private and residential aged care homes
slides.highlight: This work addresses HRI challenges in aged care settings, offering design strategies for accessibility and privacy that align with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Review of human-robot interaction challenges and design strategies for aged care environments.
card.key_idea: Frames care homes as extreme HRI settings, proposing hybrid robot-ambient systems with privacy-by-design and robust interaction modalities.
card.evaluation: Qualitative review of existing deployments and literature; proposes real-world metrics like false alarms, staff workload, and system reliability.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical validation of proposed frameworks; relies on heterogeneous prior studies without unified benchmarking standards.

slides.title: DecisionTraceBench: Tracking Decision-Critical Information in Multi-Party Spoken Conversations
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR MULTI-PARTY DECISION STATE TRACKING
slides.highlight: This benchmark evaluates joint decision evolution, speaker attribution, and temporal evidence in multi-party speech, directly addressing HyECHO's goals of modeling group norms and addressee dynamics in hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: New benchmark evaluates joint recovery of decision event chains, speaker attribution, and temporal evidence in financial speech.
card.key_idea: DecisionTraceBench uses trajectory-level F1 to score complete event-chain recovery, requiring correct actions, speakers, scope, and time intervals.
card.evaluation: Tested on Chinese financial dialogues (synthetic/human) using cascaded and direct-audio models; best DCIST score was 21.35%.
card.limitation: Limited to scripted Chinese financial dialogues; current models struggle with multi-event chains even with reference text.

slides.title: RoleHear: Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Role-Attributed Streaming Speech Recognition
slides.tldr: Streaming ASR with inline role attribution
slides.highlight: RoleHear integrates role attribution directly into streaming speech recognition using lightweight tokens and semi-supervised learning, addressing the scarcity of role labels in real-time applications.

card.one_liner: RoleHear enables low-latency, role-attributed streaming ASR via single-pass pseudo-labeling and inline role tokens.
card.key_idea: A cache-aware streaming transducer emits decoupled turn-boundary and delayed role tokens, trained via single-pass pseudo-labeling from an offline teacher.
card.evaluation: Tested on Earnings-21/22 (silver labels) and ServiceCall (gold labels); metrics include WER, RWER, and F1 against offline teachers and cascades.
card.limitation: Relies on MLLM-generated silver labels for public data, potentially introducing noise, and requires a separate offline teacher for pseudo-labeling.

slides.title: PrefO2O: Zero-Shot Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning via Offline-to-Online Latent Preference Transfer
slides.tldr: ZERO-SHOT PREFERENCE TRANSFER VIA OPTIMAL TRANSPORT
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how confidence-weighted optimal transport can align latent preference structures for zero-shot transfer in preference-based reinforcement learning, offering a mechanism to reduce human labeling costs in coadaptive loops.

card.one_liner: PrefO2O enables zero-shot preference-based RL on new tasks by transferring latent preference structures from offline source data.
card.key_idea: Learns a task-invariant latent preference space via VAE and optimal transport to generate pseudo-labels for online reward adaptation without human feedback.
card.evaluation: Tested on Meta-World, Robosuite, and DeepMind Control Suite; outperforms PEARL and PrefFew, matching oracle methods across transfer settings.
card.limitation: Requires related domain families for transferable preference structures; performance may degrade if source and target tasks lack shared behavioral patterns.

slides.title: From Voiceprints to User Entities: Online Speaker-Memory Construction for Multi-User Spoken Agents
slides.highlight: This work addresses the challenge of maintaining persistent user identities in multi-user spoken agents by treating voiceprints as evolving acoustic evidence rather than static identifiers, a capability directly relevant to HyECHO's goal of robust social perception and identity recognition in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: EvoSpeakerMem constructs persistent user entities from evolving voiceprints for accurate multi-user spoken agent memory.
card.key_idea: Training-free layer using causal speaker routing, selective acoustic-state updates, and identity-partitioned memory writes with replaceable backends.
card.evaluation: LoCoMo-ID and SMIIP-TV benchmarks; gated updates improve QA by 3.86-11.62 points over fixed representations under shifted conditions.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic voices; reveals fragmentation-contamination trade-off where updating reduces errors but risks incorrect cross-user links.

slides.title: Behavioural Quality Is Not Learning Utility: Objective Mismatch in Human Behaviour Models for Robot Learning
slides.tldr: BEHAVIOURAL FIDELITY DOES NOT GUARANTEE RL TRAINING UTILITY
slides.highlight: This study reveals that human behaviour models optimized for behavioural fidelity may not effectively support robot policy learning, highlighting a critical objective mismatch in HRI training pipelines.

card.one_liner: High behavioural realism in human models does not guarantee better downstream robot policy learning.
card.key_idea: Compares generative model metrics (FD, KL) against RL policy performance to reveal objective mismatches in HRI training.
card.evaluation: Tested on highway driving and handover using rule-based/data-driven models; metrics failed to predict policy utility consistently.
card.limitation: Results are domain-specific and sensitive to trajectory representation choices, limiting generalizability.

slides.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces a metacognitive controller for diffusion language agents that optimizes inference efficiency by adapting token generation based on environmental interaction needs, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's goal of self-monitoring and efficient AI teammates.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive controller reduces diffusion agent inference FLOPs by 20.6% while maintaining accuracy.
card.key_idea: Lightweight controller monitors interaction states to dynamically adjust active computation range and token acceptance thresholds via cascaded decoding.
card.evaluation: Tested on BFCL and multi-hop QA benchmarks; reduces FLOPs 20.6% vs baselines with competitive accuracy, validated by ablations.
card.limitation: Requires training on specific agent trajectories; adapting to evolving diffusion models remains an open challenge.

slides.title: Realbotix Launches Echo Humanoid Robot Line
slides.highlight: Realbotix has launched the Echo humanoid robot line, introducing new hardware options for embodied social interaction.

slides.title: NextEval: An Agent-Based Solver and Benchmark for Derivative-Free Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces an LLM-based agent system for derivative-free optimization, demonstrating how large language models can guide numerical tool selection and budget allocation in black-box environments. This is relevant to MIMIC as it provides a concrete example of integrating LLM-based agent models with numerical simulation tools, a core component of the project's hybrid human-AI society modeling.

card.one_liner: NextEval uses an LLM agent to guide derivative-free optimization, outperforming baselines in evaluation efficiency.
card.key_idea: An LLM agent selects numerical tools and parameters based on evaluation history, while the environment executes methods and maintains state.
card.evaluation: Tested on low-dimensional S2MPJ problems against COBYQA, NEWUOA, and Powell, showing higher aggregate scores in evaluation efficiency.
card.limitation: Limited to low-dimensional problems; gains may stem from system design rather than LLM reasoning alone, and costs are unmeasured.
